requirements.note: Newest first, grouped by day; each header shows the date ('Sun, Oct 25', 'Today', 'Yesterday') on the left and the day total right-aligned.
Summary card shows 'Spent this month $5,269.70 · 86 expenses' with a category colour strip; updates immediately after add, edit and delete.

Sheet with large amount field (decimal pad), merchant, category picker listing the 7 categories with icons, date defaulting to today, optional note. Save stays disabled for -5 / empty merchant, and an inline red message explains why. Cancel with changes asks 'Discard changes?'.
Tapping a row opens 'Edit expense' prefilled; merchant and date edits saved and the row moved to 'Yesterday'. Swiping left shows a red Delete action, which removes the row and updates the totals.

Categories tab lists this month's categories largest first (Bills $1,544.59, 29.3% of total …) with icons, share bars and chevrons; tapping one pushes that category's transactions for the month, grouped by day.
US currency throughout ($1,544.59). The added and edited expense survived a relaunch.

tells: Custom warm theme: off-white/beige background, peach summary card and orange-red tint instead of system grouped backgrounds and accent colour; looks more designed than stock iOS.
The Done button above the number pad is a floating orange capsule that partly covers the Date row.
During a swipe, the row's category icon disappears and the row turns into a separate rounded card; this is not quite how a UITableView swipe looks.
The long validation message ('…maximum $999,999,999.99') is a bit web-form-like.
A.scroll: The long list (240 rows, 38 pages) scrolls smoothly when dragged slowly, flung or pulled past the top. It had no blank rows or pop-in, and scroll position was kept after opening and cancelling an edit.

requirements.note: Newest first, grouped by day; each header is one string 'Sun, Oct 25, 2026 · $222.02', showing the date and the day total.
'THIS MONTH $5,269.70, October 2026 · 86 expenses' card at the top of the list; updates after add, edit and delete.

Stock form: amount (decimal pad), merchant, category pop-up menu with the 7 categories, date defaulting to today, note. Save (checkmark) stays disabled for -5 or no merchant, but the 'Enter an amount greater than zero.' footer is always grey and never flags the error. Cancel discards edits without asking.
Tapping a row opens 'Edit Expense' prefilled; the edit and date change were saved. Swiping left reveals Delete, which removes the row and updates the totals.
Categories tab lists categories largest first with amount, '29.3% of total · 16 expenses' and a blue bar; tapping one pushes its transactions for the month.
US currency throughout. The added and edited expense survived a relaunch.

bugs: While swiping a row left, the row turns grey and its subtitle lines (category, note) vanish, leaving only a clipped title ('e Edp') and the amount.
At the largest text size, the merchant name breaks mid-word without a hyphen ('Clim / bing Gym') because the amount stays on the same line and squeezes it.
tells: Transaction rows have almost no vertical padding: titles sit against the top edge of each cell and the note lines against the bottom, so the list looks cramped.
Category rows on the Categories screen have no disclosure chevron, even though they push a detail screen.
Day header puts the total inline after a '·' instead of right-aligned, and repeats the year on every header.
Cancelling an edited form discards changes without the usual confirmation.
The validation hint is static grey text and never turns into an error state.
B.scroll: The long list scrolls and flings smoothly, with no blank rows or jumps, and keeps its position after an edit is cancelled. The cramped row padding makes it feel dense.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist data. A is noticeably more finished: comfortable row metrics, icons, a discard confirmation, clear validation errors, and a layout that adapts well at the largest text size. B uses stock SwiftUI controls but has cramped rows, a glitchy swipe animation, and a mid-word break at large text; A's custom warm theme is its main departure from a stock iOS look.
